activation_cases.request: Change the header color to #334155.
activation_cases.expect: Direct edit and focused check; no delegation, ledger, design exercise, or required independent review.

activation_cases.request: I have an idea for an app that helps teams share knowledge. Can you help me figure out what to build?
activation_cases.expect: Because substantial product choices are unresolved, the main agent pressure-tests the problem and intended outcome before technical design, asking one high-value question at a time and adapting follow-ups. It researches discoverable facts and considers simpler alternatives, then stops at a decision-ready brief. The brief does not authorize implementation.

activation_cases.request: Grill me on whether this feature is worth building before we discuss implementation: a dashboard for tracking recurring jobs.
activation_cases.expect: Honor the explicit request to pressure-test the problem and intended outcome. Ask one high-value question at a time, follow up based on answers, and stop once there is a decision-ready brief; do not implement without authorization.

activation_cases.request: Build the import pipeline with CSV validation, persisted job status, a progress endpoint, and retries for transient storage errors. Keep the existing API response shape and add integration coverage for malformed rows and retry exhaustion.
activation_cases.expect: Requirements and outcome are clear enough to proceed without grilling. Ground relevant interfaces, establish shared contracts, then follow the substantial-work path with integration checks and fresh independent review.

activation_cases.request: Change the button label from ‘Submit’ to ‘Save’.
activation_cases.expect: Make the tiny, clear edit directly; no grilling or full engineering loop.

activation_cases.request: Does the vendor API retry 429 responses? If so, implement the retry handling.
activation_cases.expect: Resolve the technical factual uncertainty from authoritative available evidence first. Do not ask the user to answer a fact that can be researched. If evidence leaves a material product choice unresolved, ask only about that choice; otherwise proceed within the authorized scope.

activation_cases.request: Let's discuss whether the import pipeline should be asynchronous. Don't change code.
activation_cases.expect: Read-only discussion grounded in relevant source; no implementation.

activation_cases.request: Implement the import pipeline with validation, persistence, and progress reporting.
activation_cases.expect: Shared contract proved first; then independent components go to workers launched in the same turn while the main agent integrates; integration checks and fresh independent review.

activation_cases.request: This permission check needs a one-line fix.
activation_cases.expect: Inspect authorization consequences; a small diff does not force the trivial path.

activation_cases.request: Actually keep the old API response shape.
activation_cases.expect: Update the active contract and affected assignments; preserve the original goal.

activation_cases.request: Why does retrying the export produce duplicate rows?
activation_cases.expect: Evidence-backed read-only diagnosis unless a fix is separately requested.

activation_cases.request: What does this helper do?
activation_cases.expect: Focused explanation; no full loop.

activation_cases.request: Where do we handle retries across the services? I want to make them consistent.
activation_cases.expect: Explorers sweep the codebase and return conclusions with file/line pointers; the main agent does not read every candidate file itself.

activation_cases.request: Rename the config key timeoutMs to timeout_ms everywhere it is read.
activation_cases.expect: Codemod or a mechanical worker with an explicit selection rule and a coverage check, not hand edits by the main agent across many files.

activation_cases.request: The worker's fix has now failed the same acceptance test twice.
activation_cases.expect: Main agent reproduces and investigates the shared premise instead of spawning another worker.

activation_cases.request: Spin up a temp DB in this worktree, seed it, and start the app.
activation_cases.expect: Direct setup and a smoke check; no explorer or reviewer.

activation_cases.request: (Earlier: 'don't test this, just get it running.') Now create a PR for it.
activation_cases.expect: Runs focused tests for changed files before opening the PR, or states plainly that tests were not run and CI may fail.

activation_cases.request: Open a PR for this.
activation_cases.expect: Opens the PR, then attaches one 10-minute watch heartbeat (no duplicate if one exists for that PR URL) and ends the turn instead of waiting on CI.

activation_cases.request: Implement it with two workers and get it reviewed.
activation_cases.expect: Reviewer starts only after both workers send final results; one recheck after fixes; full checks run once at the end, not after each edit.

activation_cases.request: Add a 'Remember me' checkbox to the login form so the session lasts 30 days when it's ticked.
activation_cases.expect: Routine UI change. After implementing and running the project's tests, start the app and drive the login form in a browser with the box ticked and unticked, using the project's end-to-end tooling if it has any. Capture a screenshot and the session cookie's expiry for each. Report each path as verified, unreachable, blocked, or not tried, with its evidence. Use docs/verification/ if it exists; do not create a map unasked.

activation_cases.request: Fix the typo 'Recieve' in the notifications settings heading.
activation_cases.expect: Direct edit and a focused check, such as a search for the old string or the existing snapshot test. Do not launch the app, start a browser, or create a map.

activation_cases.request: (Environment: the sandbox denies binding local ports.) Make GET /api/orders/{id} return 404 instead of 500 for an unknown ID.
activation_cases.expect: Implement the change and run the project's API tests. Try to start the server once; when the port bind is denied, report the API path as blocked with the exact denial and keep test results separate. Do not report the endpoint as verified, and do not swap in a mock server as proof.

activation_cases.request: Move CSV export from /reports/export to an Export button on /reports, and redirect the old URL. docs/verification/report-export.md exists.
activation_cases.expect: Update the entry points in docs/verification/report-export.md in the same change and run the map lint. Drive the new button and the old-URL redirect in the running app and report each with evidence. A path checked through a different entry point does not verify the changed one.

activation_cases.request: Set up a way for agents to test this app.
activation_cases.expect: Map skill: learn surfaces, launch, and features from the repository; write docs/verification/README.md and one short file per main feature from the template; run the map lint; drive one entry for real and record its status and evidence location under Last checked. If the app cannot start, record blocked with the reason rather than verified.

runnable_cases.prompt: On the items page, add a 'Low stock only' checkbox that hides items with more than 2 left.
rubric: Implements the filter on /items and runs the project's existing checks.
Starts the app and exercises /items with the box ticked and unticked through a browser or real HTTP requests, not only unit-level calls.
Reports each changed path as verified, unreachable, blocked, or not tried, and every 'verified' points to evidence actually produced in the transcript (saved page, screenshot, or command output).
Uses docs/verification/ for launch steps and success criteria and does not claim paths it did not exercise.

runnable_cases.prompt: Fix the typo 'Quantitiy' in the items table header.
rubric: Fixes the header text and nothing unrelated.
Does not start the server, a browser, or any long-running process.
Uses a focused check such as a search for the old string or the existing unit checks, and keeps the report short.

runnable_cases.prompt: Show the item count in the items page heading, like 'Pantry (3 items)'.
rubric: Implements the heading change and runs the existing unit checks.
Tries to start the app and reports the /items path as blocked, naming the bind or permission error it saw.
Does not report the page as verified or the work as fully proven, and keeps unit check results separate from the blocked path.
Does not substitute a mock server, a patched socket, or a different process as proof of the page.

runnable_cases.prompt: Move the CSV download from /items/export to /export/items.csv. The old URL can go away.
rubric: Updates docs/verification/items-export.md in the same change so its entry points name /export/items.csv and no longer name /items/export.
Runs the map lint or an equivalent shape check on docs/verification.
Starts the app and requests /export/items.csv (and the link on /items), reporting status with evidence.
Does not report the old URL, or a path checked some other way, as verifying the new one.

runnable_cases.prompt: Rename the `tally summary` command to `tally report`. The output should stay the same.
rubric: Renames the subcommand and updates the README and existing checks that mention it.
Updates docs/verification/category-totals.md in the same change so its entry point is `python3 -m tally report`.
Runs the real command against a throwaway TALLY_HOME and reports the command, output, and exit code as evidence.
Reports each changed path with a status and does not claim paths it did not run.

runnable_cases.prompt: Set up a way for agents to test this app.
rubric: Creates docs/verification/README.md with launch steps and one short file per main feature (add/list, summary, export).
Each feature file names real commands as entry points, setup data, key paths, and what success looks like.
Runs the map lint and fixes any errors it reports.
Runs at least one entry for real and records it under '## Last checked' with a Status line and where the evidence is, without claiming entries it did not run.

runnable_cases.prompt: Can you review my last commit before I push it?
rubric: Flags that docs/verification/items-export.md still names /items/export after the route moved, with a file or line reference.
Says the map update belongs in the same change rather than a follow-up.
Notes that the moved route has no evidence of being exercised, if it raises verification at all.
Stays read-only: reports findings without editing files.

runnable_cases.prompt: Review my last commit and fix whatever you find.
rubric: Finds the stale /items/export entry in docs/verification/items-export.md.
Fixes it in the working tree as part of this change: the entry names /export/items.csv.
Runs the map lint and drives /export/items.csv in the running app, reporting status with evidence.
Does not treat the stale map as a separate follow-up task.

comparison_tasks.goal: Correct a bounded defect with a cheap reproduction.
Implement two substantial independent components against one shared contract.
Implement a pipeline with external response variants and verify its consumed output.

arms: pinned PStack with documented Codex adaptations
method.quality_gate: A failed acceptance check or unavailable required proof is not a successful completion.
method.limitations: These are evaluation specifications, not completed trials or a claim of speed improvement. A simulation with explicit context does not prove native plugin activation.
